rootCause: `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:14` imports `resolvePinnedCurrency` from `lib/display-currency-context.tsx`, which is a `'use client'` module (directive at `lib/display-currency-context.tsx:29`), and then **calls** it as a plain function at `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:219` (`const pinnedCurrency = resolvePinnedCurrency(preferredCurrency, currencyOrgKey !== null)`) inside an async Server Component. In the RSC/server bundle, Next's `next-flight-loader` does not ship the real module: it replaces every named export of a `'use client'` file with a client reference whose implementation is `function() { throw new Error("Attempted to call resolvePinnedCurrency() from the server but resolvePinnedCurrency is on the client...") }` (see `node_modules/next/dist/build/webpack/loaders/next-flight-loader/index.js:126-134`). Line 219 is unconditional and sits in the layout that wraps every route in the `(dashboard)` group, so the very first thing every signed-in dashboard page does after auth is throw — producing the identical "Application error: a server-side exception has occurred" with one shared digest (1095162490) on every page. It passed every gate because `tsc` resolves the real module's types, Vitest imports it in Node where `'use client'` is an inert string (`lib/__tests__/display-currency-pin.test.ts` tests the function directly), and `next build` never prerenders the layout (it awaits Clerk auth + `cookies()`, so it is dynamic). Critically, the breaking call was introduced in the *review-fix* commit `d4628468`, not in `9532b044` — at `9532b044` the layout imported only `DisplayCurrencyProvider` (a component, which is the legal way to cross the boundary) and resolved the currency inline. That is why the "client walk / headless QA" recorded in `9532b044`'s message passed and the merge shipped broken.
evidence: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:14 (at c14169bc) — `import { DisplayCurrencyProvider, resolvePinnedCurrency } from '@/lib/display-currency-context'`; a server component importing a value (not a component) across the client boundary.

app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:219 (at c14169bc) — `const pinnedCurrency = resolvePinnedCurrency(preferredCurrency, currencyOrgKey !== null)`. Unconditional: it runs for admins, clients and previews alike, on every render of the (dashboard) layout.

lib/display-currency-context.tsx:29 — `'use client'` (first statement after the header comment). `resolvePinnedCurrency` is defined at line 124 and `asCurrencyCode` at line 105 of the same client module.

node_modules/next/dist/build/webpack/loaders/next-flight-loader/index.js:126-134 — for each named export of a client module the server bundle emits `export const <ref> = registerClientReference(function() { throw new Error("Attempted to call <ref>() from the server but <ref> is on the client. It's not possible to invoke a client function from the server, it can only be rendered as a Component or passed to props of a Client Component.") }, ...)`. Calling it throws; there is no build-time diagnostic.

`git show 9532b044:"app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx"` line 14 imports only `DisplayCurrencyProvider`, and lines 192-208 resolve `pinnedCurrency` inline with no cross-boundary call. The breaking line arrived in d4628468 ("client walk review fixes"), which was merged as 465a490d two minutes later without re-running the live walk.

Why the build/tests were green: `npm run build` is plain `next build` (package.json scripts) and the layout is dynamic (awaits `getViewAudience()` → Clerk `auth()` + `cookies()`), so it is never prerendered; `lib/__tests__/display-currency-pin.test.ts:13` imports `resolvePinnedCurrency` in a Node test env where the directive is ignored.
Blast radius matches exactly: `app/(auth)/sign-in` does not go through `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, which is why /sign-in stayed 200 while every dashboard page died.

404s are NOT a regression, part 1: there is no `/api/health` route in the repo at either commit. `git ls-tree -r e3b3a4a2 -- app/api/health` and the same at c14169bc are both empty; the only health route is `app/api/admin/health/route.ts`. `/api/health` 404s by definition.

404s are NOT a regression, part 2: `node_modules/@clerk/nextjs/dist/esm/server/protect.js:17-20` — `auth.protect()` on an unauthenticated request calls `redirectToSignIn()` only `if (isPageRequest(request))`, otherwise `notFound()`. `isPageRequest` (same file, line 77) requires `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document|iframe`, `Accept: text/html`, or a Next internal-navigation header. A bare `fetch`/`curl` has none of these, so it gets Clerk's `notFound()` → 404, never the sign-in redirect. A real browser navigation still redirects.

404s are NOT a regression, part 3: the middleware diff (`middleware.ts` +14/-6) is entirely *after* `await auth.protect()` and only touches the authenticated admin-only-route branch. For an unauthenticated request the middleware is byte-identical at e3b3a4a2 and c14169bc, and the matcher was untouched. The only thing this merge changed about the 404 is its body: `app/not-found.tsx` now renders the branded panel instead of Next's built-in page. Same status code.
otherHazards: Stale/forged preview cookie locks admins out of the /clients tree. middleware.ts:222-228 now bounces `/clients|/reports|/time|/team|/docs` whenever `tahi-impersonate-org` is merely present (`!isAdmin || previewingClient`), with no validation that the value names a real org and no `isAdmin` check on the cookie itself. The cookie is browser-wide and long-lived; the only way out is the Exit preview button, which renders from the layout that was crashing. Fixing the crash re-enables the escape hatch, but the trap remains if the banner ever fails to mount.

Two divergent definitions of "previewing". `middleware.ts:222` honours the cookie regardless of session org; `lib/view-audience.ts:resolveViewAudience` deliberately ignores it for non-admins (`previewOrgId = isAdmin ? cookieOrgId : null`). Harmless today (a non-admin already trips `!isAdmin`) but the two will drift.

New blocking D1 read on the hottest path. app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:199-218 adds a sequential `organisations` lookup to every client-audience dashboard render, keyed with `or(eq(clerkOrgId, k), eq(id, k))` — an OR across two columns, and `clerkOrgId` is not guaranteed to be indexed. It is correctly wrapped in try/catch so a D1 failure degrades rather than throws, but it works against the perf work recorded in project_perf_audit_2026_06_29.

`format()` silently changed shape for pinned clients. lib/display-currency-context.tsx now returns `formatNativeWithDisplay(amount, 'NZD')` — a two-currency string like "NZ$1,500 ≈ US$882" — from what every caller treats as a single formatted number. Every KPI tile, table cell and plan card on a client surface that calls `format()` will get a ~2x longer string. Not a crash; a layout/overflow regression that needs a 375px pass before this is re-landed.

app/(dashboard)/not-found.tsx renders *inside* the dashboard layout, so any future layout throw also takes out the branded 404 (and `/sitemap`'s new `notFound()` for previews at app/(dashboard)/sitemap/page.tsx:20). Consider whether the studio 404 should sit above the data-fetching layout.

Process hazard, the real one. CLAUDE.md rule 8 (Definition of Done) items 4-6 require a live browser smoke on the deployed URL before a task flips to done. `9532b044`'s message documents a client walk; `d4628468` and `c14169bc` document only type-check / lint / vitest / next build, and `d4628468` is the commit that introduced the fault. One page load against the deploy would have caught it. Any re-land of this branch must smoke the deployed URL after the LAST commit, not the first.

Same class of bug is one edit away elsewhere. `lib/use-homepage-motion.ts`, `lib/use-mentions.ts` and `lib/use-user-preference.ts` are also `'use client'` modules under lib/ whose names read like plain utilities. A lint rule would be cheap insurance (see fix).
fix:
Minimal safe change, two lines of movement and no behaviour change: move `BASE_CURRENCY`, `asCurrencyCode` and `resolvePinnedCurrency` out of `lib/display-currency-context.tsx` into the existing server-safe `lib/currency.ts` (it has no `'use client'`, and already owns `SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES` and the `CurrencyCode` type, which are the only things those three functions need). Then: `lib/display-currency-context.tsx` re-imports `asCurrencyCode` from `@/lib/currency` for its own internal `asCurrencyCode(pinned)` call; `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:14` splits its import into `import { DisplayCurrencyProvider } from '@/lib/display-currency-context'` plus `import { resolvePinnedCurrency } from '@/lib/currency'`; `lib/__tests__/display-currency-pin.test.ts:13` retargets to `@/lib/currency`. Nothing else changes — `<DisplayCurrencyProvider pinned={pinnedCurrency}>` still receives the same value.

If you want the smallest possible revert-and-reland instead, drop the server-side call entirely and go back to what `9532b044` shipped and QA'd: pass the raw string through (`<DisplayCurrencyProvider pinned={preferredCurrency} isClientAudience={currencyOrgKey !== null}>`) and let the provider — which is already a client component and already calls `asCurrencyCode(pinned)` internally — do the resolution. That deletes line 219 and the cross-boundary import outright.

Verification that must run before re-landing, in this order: (1) `npm run build`, then (2) `npm run preview` (`opennextjs-cloudflare build && opennextjs-cloudflare preview`) and load `/overview` signed in — the workers preview exercises the same server bundle that broke, which `next build` alone does not; (3) after deploy, a real browser navigation to `/overview` and `/clients` signed in, and a logged-out browser hit on `/overview` expecting the 307 to `/sign-in`. Do not re-measure the logged-out case with bare `curl`/`fetch`: without `Accept: text/html` Clerk answers 404 by design, which is what produced the phantom second symptom in this incident.

Cheap guard against recurrence: add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule (or a Vitest source-scan in the style of the new `lib/__tests__/studio-page-audience.test.ts`) that fails when a file under `app/**` without `'use client'` imports any non-component symbol from a module whose first statement is `'use client'`.
